evaluation_claims.text: Solar photovoltaic panels are one of the most vital clean energy technologies.
Solar thermal collectors harness heat from the Sun to warm water for heating or domestic use, whereas photovoltaic panels convert solar radiation directly into electricity.
The photovoltaic effect is the ability of certain semiconductor materials to produce electricity when exposed to light.
When sunlight strikes a semiconductor material in a photovoltaic cell, the energy of incoming photons excites electric charges (electrons) and causes them to move.
The movement of charges in a photovoltaic cell generates both voltage and electric current.
A solar panel contains photovoltaic cells together with protective elements that ensure durability and functionality.
Electricity generated directly by photovoltaic cells is direct current (DC).
Direct current can charge batteries or run DC-compatible devices, while transmission networks and homes rely on alternating current (AC).
An inverter converts DC into AC so the electricity can be consumed immediately, stored, or fed into the power grid.
A panel's electricity-generating capacity increases with its surface area or the number of cells in it.
Individual panels can be linked into arrays ranging from two panels to hundreds of modules.
Photovoltaic systems are used in applications ranging from water pumps and individual homes to utility-scale electricity generation.
Commercial panel efficiency progressed from under ten percent in the mid-1980s to around fifteen percent in 2015, and is now approaching twenty-five percent for state-of-the-art modules.
Experimental and niche cells for satellites have achieved nearly fifty percent efficiency.
Solar panels produce the most electricity when directly facing the Sun.
Some systems use tracking mechanisms that follow the Sun's path, but these systems are expensive.
Most installations use fixed panels angled to balance physical and economic performance, typically facing south in the Northern Hemisphere and north in the Southern Hemisphere.
Solar irradiance is the single most significant factor affecting photovoltaic output and has strong geographic and temporal variations.
Clouds, pollutants, aerosols, and dust can substantially reduce photovoltaic electricity generation, with output reductions of up to sixty percent, particularly in arid desert regions.
Elevated module temperatures reduce photovoltaic efficiency by 0.4 to 0.5 percent for every degree Celsius increase in temperature.
Higher ground albedo boosts photovoltaic output through reflected light, while snow accumulation can obstruct panels.
Hailstorms and wildfires can inflict substantial damage on photovoltaic systems, and solar eclipses cause large, short-lived output drops.

reference_verifications.rationale: Evidence says solar energy is one of the most important energy sources and PV expansion is central to the energy transition, and PV is clean; but 'one of the most vital clean energy technologies' is not stated verbatim.
Directly states both panel types and their functions.
Defines the effect as the ability of certain materials to produce electricity when exposed to light; semiconductor is mentioned in the same passage.
Photon energy hitting a semiconductor triggers movement of electric charges; electrons gain energy and move.
States that this movement creates voltage and current.
Panel has cells plus other elements that protect and guarantee functionality and durability.
PV cells generate DC electricity.
DC can charge batteries powering DC devices; nearly all electricity in transmission/distribution is AC; inverters yield AC for homes. 'Run DC-compatible devices' is roughly covered.
Inverter converts DC to AC; electricity can be consumed, stored or fed into the grid.
Capacity increases with number of cells or surface area.
Array can be as few as two panels to hundreds.
Water pumps, individual homes, utility-scale generation.
Matches efficiency progression exactly.
Experimental and niche cells such as satellites reached nearly 50%.
PV cells and panels produce the most electricity when directly facing the sun.
EIA says tracking systems keep panels facing the sun, but are expensive.
Most PV systems are fixed, usually south in the northern hemisphere and north in the southern, at an angle that optimizes physical and economic performance.
Irradiance has strong geographic and temporal variability, making it the most significant factor.
Atmospheric conditions (clouds, aerosols, pollutants, dust) can reduce output by up to 60%, especially in desert regions.
Raising module temperature reduces efficiency by 0.4–0.5% per degree Celsius.
Evidence says terrain factors like albedo and snow have mixed effects, with increased reflection boosting output but snow obstructing panels.
Evidence states wildfires and hailstorms cause substantial damage, while solar eclipses lead to large but short-lived output losses.

additional_metric_details.notes: All scores are Claude judgments, not verified ground truth. Repair effectiveness compares coverage/narration, not factual truth. No revision or no retrieval is N/A rather than zero.

metric_semantics.reference_evidence_support_percent: Evidence entailment within the frozen reference corpus; not factual accuracy.
metric_semantics.query_coverage_percent: Coverage of a fixed six-aspect checklist derived once per question from the question text and shared by all systems; missing/duplicate judge outputs are normalized against that fixed denominator.
metric_semantics.narration_input: Coverage, relevance, narration and grounded-requirement judgements use the complete script with [E-...] evidence markers removed; claim extraction and citation metrics use the marked script. Aspect scores are continuous in [0, 1].
metric_semantics.narration_quality_percent: Ten-dimension spoken educational narration score; excludes factual truth.
metric_semantics.citation_precision: Share of emitted citation IDs that are identified as supporting the claim when verification is restricted to cited passages.
metric_semantics.citation_recall: Share of all citation-required extracted factual claims that have at least one cited passage judged to support the claim.
